description: Daily proactive status card. Sourced from ALL THREE monitors - the 2026-08-13 card said '9/9 healthy' from the snapshot probe alone while a camera stood 185h past its motion-staleness window on the same panel. 'Probes OK' is the honest claim: the probe measures the snapshot path, not motion-event delivery. 2026-08-30: now sourced from ALL FOUR monitors (cam_vision was missing entirely, and it is the one with no dead-man). Each line carries its own NOT REPORTING fallback. The motion guard used to test stale_count is none, but cam_motion.py's fail() path leaves stale_count at 0, so a monitor that had just failed rendered as the affirmative all-clear "0 camera(s) beyond their staleness window"; it now tests error and hours_since, which do go null on that path. A BOOT TRIGGER was added because a bare 08:00 time trigger means any restart after 08:00 erases the only proactive positive signal for the rest of the day, and its absence is indistinguishable from a healthy fleet - it went silently missing on 3 of the 7 days to 2026-08-30. 2026-10-27: the boot card rendered a probe that ran before the camera engine had started. The Supervisor starts application add-ons, Scrypted among them, only once Core reports RUNNING, which is after this trigger fires, so after a host reboot (an OS update) the first probe failed on all 9 cameras; the card fired 5 s before the Scrypted container was started and its summary began 'FLEET-MISS: 9/9 probes failed this cycle | 0/9 OK', while the next probe two minutes later was 9/9 OK. On the boot trigger the card now waits for a probe reading with no failed probe (state not -1, miss_count 0) and a visual monitor that reports no camera unseen (blind_count 0), then posts with '(after a restart)' in its footer. The vision condition matters after a long outage: vision's run from before the engine came up reports every camera NOT SEEN >15m, and its run on the first good probe cycle lands seconds after the probe's. A missing attribute, as on an unknown sensor, keeps the card waiting. The wait is capped at 7 minutes, which always spans three probe cycles after the trigger (the first probe runs during setup, before the trigger, the 120 s timer starts from it, and a probe can run for its 30 s command timeout) and the vision run that follows; at the cap the card posts whatever the monitors read, so a real outage still reaches it. A wait on the sensor's next state change instead would end on the next probe whatever it read. The 08:00 card does not wait; an 08:00 trigger that lands during a boot wait is dropped (mode single, max_exceeded silent) and the boot card stands in for it.

then.wait_template: {{ states('sensor.camera_health') | int(-1) >= 0 and state_attr('sensor.camera_health', 'miss_count') | int(-1) == 0 and state_attr('sensor.camera_visual_activity', 'blind_count') | int(-1) == 0 }}

data.title: 📷 Camera health
